messages:
alex: Heads up — after merge 0f3a9c the INT8 serving job on canary showed a +18% p99 token latency. CI perf job flagged it: https://ci.internal/runs/8921 :alert:
maya: ugh, saw that metric. Is this the dequant hotpath or kernel selector flipping?
liam: I ran a quick profile on the canary pod. Dequant memcpy time jumped. Flamegraph attached (snippet):
```
  dequant::apply()  42%
  memcpy           31%
  kernel_select    8%
  kv_cache_miss    6%
```
sam: interesting — memcpy up suggests an extra copy path. Any recent changes around buffer layout or zero-copy?
liam: merge 0f3a9c replaced the flat buffer view with a ref-counted slice wrapper and added an alignment step. suspect that alignment causes a fallback copy in the int8 dequant path.
maya: can we reproduce locally with a small repro? maybe run perf-ci job with perf-opts `--seq-len 128 --batch 4` and the int8 profile.
alex: started a bisect job: `scripts/perf_bisect --range=0f1..0f3a9c --target=canary-int8` — will post results.
perf-bot: perf-ci triggered: build 8922 queued (bisect step 1/6).
liam: quick hack: forced the slice wrapper to expose raw pointer (bypass alignment) and latency goes back to baseline in local run. So copy avoidance matters.
sam: run the kv cache microbench too; increased copies amplify KV lookup latency because we're touching more pages.
maya: given this is a canary regression and affects p99, propose holding rollout and reverting the merge if bisect isolates it.
alex: agreed. if bisect points at 0f3a9c we should revert and follow up with a proper zero-copy plan.
deploy-bot: canary rollout paused for merge 0f3a9c (manual hold).
liam: next steps: 1) finish bisect, 2) confirm with kv microbench and real traffic replay, 3) revert if reproducible. I'll push a bisect summary by EOD.
maya: also add a unit test that fails when extra copies occur (compare mem allocations count in stress harness).
alex: thanks — tagging @product and @sre for awareness of potential transient latency bump.
perf-bot: bisect complete: culprit commit 0f3a9c (slice alignment change). Estimated rollback safe.
alex: rolling back now and re-running CI.
maya: nice catch — we'll follow up with a design doc on safe zero-copy wrappers that preserve kernel selector hooks. :thumbsup:
liam: saved traces are in /mnt/perf/traces/3461234567-canary-run-8922, added notes in the PR thread.
sam: happy path team — once reverted we should run a controlled A/B to validate p50/p99 across 24h.
alex: re-run CI shows p99 back to baseline. closing hold and will open postmortem with action items.
maya: postmortem checklist: root cause, mechanism (alignment->copy), test coverage, docs for wrapper semantics, and follow-up ticket for kernel selector integration.

-- end of thread --
